import urllib.request, urllib.parse, time, re
BASE = "https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi"

def post(params):
    data = urllib.parse.urlencode(params).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE, data=data, headers={"User-Agent":"biomni-client"})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180).read().decode()

seq = "GTGAGCCACCGCGCCCGGCC"

 "CMD":"Put",

 "MEGABLAST":"on",
 "DATABASE":"core_nt",
 "QUERY":seq,
 "WORD_SIZE":"20",
 "EXPECT":"1000",
 "HITLIST_SIZE":"100",
 "ENTREZ_QUERY":"Homo sapiens[Organism]",
 "FILTER":"F",
}
try:
    r = post(params)
    rid = re.search(r"RID = (\S+)", r)
    rtoe = re.search(r"RTOE = (\d+)", r)
    print("RID:", rid.group(1) if rid else None, "RTOE:", rtoe.group(1) if rtoe else None)

import urllib.request, urllib.parse, time, re
BASE = "https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi"
def get(params):
    url = BASE + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent":"biomni-client"})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180).read().decode()

RID = "ENPJARWH014"
status = None
for i in range(40):
    r = get({"CMD":"Get","FORMAT_OBJECT":"SearchInfo","RID":RID})
    m = re.search(r"Status=(\w+)", r)
    status = m.group(1) if m else "UNKNOWN"
    hits = re.search(r"ThereAreHits=(\w+)", r)
    print(i, status, hits.group(1) if hits else "")
    if status in ("READY","FAILED","UNKNOWN","EXPIRED"):
        break
    time.sleep(15)
print("FINAL STATUS:", status)

content.text:
## What this sequence actually is

Your primer has **no single location** in the human genome. Its reverse complement is `GGCCGGGCGCGGTGGCTCAC`, which is the first 20 nt of the **Alu consensus** — so this is an Alu-targeting (inter-Alu PCR) primer, annealing at the 5′ end of Alu SINE elements.

**How I established that:**

1. **NCBI BLAST** (`blast_sequence`, then the BLAST URL API, RID `ENPJARWH014`, megablast, word size 20, restricted to *Homo sapiens*): 164 hits, **every one 100% identity over 20/20**, scattered across unrelated BAC clones (AC280089.1, AC279543.1, CU207370.12 …), RefSeqGene records and mRNAs. Note the E-value is only 0.092 — a 20-mer carries too little information for BLAST E-values to mean much, which is why the first default-parameter BLAST returned a nonsense macaque hit at E = 11.5. The flat 164-hit-all-perfect pattern is the real signal.

2. **Direct counting in hg38 sequence** (downloaded chr1 and chr21 FASTA from `hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/chromosomes/`, exact string search both strands, run in the Python tool):
   - chr21: **247** perfect 20/20 sites (1 per 162 kb of non-N sequence)
   - chr1: **1,699** perfect 20/20 sites (1 per 136 kb)
   - Genome-wide extrapolation from those 270 Mb: **~21,000 perfect binding sites**
   - Allowing one mismatch (still primes efficiently): 993 sites on chr21 → **~73,000 genome-wide**

3. **Repeat annotation** (UCSC REST API, `rmsk` track, hg38): I sampled 25 of the chr21 sites. All 25 overlap a RepeatMasker **SINE/Alu** element, and in all 25 the match coincides within 5 bp with the element's 5′ edge. Subfamilies hit include AluY (10/25), AluSx1, AluYb8, AluYb9, AluJb, AluSg7, AluSx, AluSq2, AluYe5, AluYf1, AluYk4, AluSx3, AluSg.

Example concrete coordinates (hg38, 1-based, with the orientation of the underlying Alu):

| Coordinates | Alu |
|---|---|
| chr21:5,010,956-5,010,975 (+) | AluJb |
| chr21:5,301,105-5,301,124 (+) | AluYb8 |
| chr21:6,463,037-6,463,056 (+) | AluJb |
| chr21:6,465,138-6,465,157 (+) | AluSc |
| chr21:6,491,880-6,491,899 (−) | AluSg7 |
| chr21:6,525,328-6,525,347 (−) | AluYb8 |

Caveats: the ~21,000 figure is an extrapolation from 270 Mb (9% of the genome) to a 2.95 Gb non-N genome; chr1 and chr21 differ in Alu density (136 vs 162 kb per site), so treat it as order-of-magnitude (~2 × 10⁴), not exact. The per-chromosome counts for chr1 and chr21 are exact. Interpretation, not computation: primers at the Alu 5′ edge point outward into flanking unique DNA, which is the standard inter-Alu / Alu-PCR design — so if this came from an Alu-PCR or fingerprinting protocol it is behaving as intended. If you meant it as a locus-specific primer, it will not work.

## ANSWER

**It does not sit at one place.** `GTGAGCCACCGCGCCCGGCC` is the reverse complement of the Alu consensus 5′ end (`GGCCGGGCGCGGTGGCTCAC`) and binds the 5′ edge of Alu SINE elements genome-wide: **1,699 perfect sites on chr1, 247 on chr21, ~21,000 estimated genome-wide in hg38** (~73,000 allowing 1 mismatch). All 25 sampled sites are annotated SINE/Alu by UCSC RepeatMasker (hg38). Example site: chr21:5,010,956-5,010,975 (AluJb). No unique chromosome/coordinate assignment is possible.
